## What We Did

Set up the portfolio workflow: made a repository from a template, cloned it with
GitHub Desktop, edited files in RStudio, rendered with Quarto, and published to
GitHub Pages.

## Key Concepts

Three places a file can live:

1. **My computer** — where I edit
2. **GitHub.com** — where it's stored
3. **My live site** — what the world sees

The loop: **Edit → Save → Render → Commit → Push → wait → refresh**

## Proving R Works

The chunk below runs when this page renders. If you can see a result underneath
it on your published site, R and Quarto are talking to each other correctly.


::: {.cell}


## Reflection

**What I want out of this course:** I want to get comfortable turning raw
urban data into analyses that support real policy decisions — especially
working with Census data in R and building a public portfolio I can show to
employers.

**One thing I'm nervous about:** the whole toolchain (R, Quarto, Git) is new
to me, and I'm worried about breaking something I don't understand when a
push doesn't look the way I expected. My plan is to just run the loop every
week until it feels normal.
